questions.question: Why is packing important in garment export?
questions.solution_html:
• Export documents are prepared by the exporter based on the buyer’s order and the requirements of customs
  • and shipping authorities. Important documents include the commercial invoice, packing list, shipping bill
  • certificate of origin, and bill of lading.
  • Incoterms.
  •  Order Quantity
  • The Order quantity is mean by the total number of garments ordered by the buyer.
  • It indicates the production volume required for a particular style, colour or size range. Large orders allow
  • fixed expenses such as sampling, production setup and overheads to be distributed over more garments.
  • Larger quantities generally reduce the cost per garment through economies of scale, while small orders may
  • have a higher unit cost.
  •  Incoterms
  • International trade terms that define the responsibilities, costs and risks of the buyer and seller during
  • transportation of goods.
  • Incoterms determine who pays for transportation, insurance, export/import clearance, customs duties and
  • delivery. They are important when calculating the final export price or landed cost.
  • FOB,CIF,EWX,DDP these are the common Incoterms.
  • Visual Merchandising
  • • Visual merchandising is the art and science of presenting products attractively to customers.
  • • It focuses on improving the appearance of products and retail stores.
  • • It helps attract customers and influence purchasing decisions.
  • • It creates an appealing shopping environment.
  • Drill Marking
  • Drill marking is the process of making small holes
  • or marks at specific positions on fabric pieces using
  • a drill or marking tool. These marks serve as
  • accurate reference points for sewing and
  • assembling garment components, such as pocket
  • placement, darts, button positions and other details.

questions.final_answer: placement, darts, button positions and other details.

questions.question: Mention four purposes of fabric inspection
questions.solution_html:
•  4 - POINT SYSTEM
  • The 4-Point System is a widely used method for evaluating and grading fabric quality based on the size of
  • defects. It is commonly used in garment and textile industries for both supplier inspection and incoming fabric
  • inspection.
  • The Main Principle is bigger the defect, the higher the penalty points.
  • A single defect is assigned a maximum of 4 penalty points based on its size.
  • Point Allocation
  • Size of defect Points
  • Up to 3 inches 1 point
  • Over 3 – 6 inches 2 points
  • Over 6 – 9 inches 3 points
  • Over 9 inches 4 points
  •  10 - POINT SYSTEM
  • The 10-Point System is a traditional method of evaluating and grading fabric quality based on the size and
  • severity of fabric defects. It is mainly used for inspecting and grading woven fabrics, particularly in textile and
  • garment industries.
  • The Main Principle is that larger defects are given higher penalty points because they have a greater effect
  • on fabric quality.
  • A defect is assigned penalty points according to its length/size, with a maximum of 10 points for a single
  • defect.
  • Point Allocation
  • Size of defect Points
  • Up to 1 inch 1 point
  • Over 1 – 5 inches 3 points
  • Over 5 – 10 inches 5 points
  • Over 10 inches 10 points
questions.source_exam: Official Model Question Paper (FYUGP 2024
questions.final_answer: Over 10 inches 10 points

questions.question: Explain the steps involved in payment through a documentary LC.
questions.solution_html:
• A Letter of Credit (L/C) is a payment method in which the buyer’s bank guarantees payment to the exporter
  • when the exporter fulfil the conditions mentioned in the L/C and submits the required documents.
  • In garment exports, the buyer opens the L/C through their bank, and the exporter manufactures and ships
  • the garments. After shipment, the exporter submits documents such as the commercial invoice, packing list
  • and Bill of Lading to the bank. The bank checks the documents and makes payment according to the L/C
  • terms.
  • L/C may be Sight L/C, where payment is made immediately after document verification, or Usance L/C
  • where payment is made after an agreed period.
  • Essays

questions.question: Explain position marking (drill marking) and bundle ticketing used in the preparation for sewing.
questions.solution_html:
• For the materials are prepare before sewing its gone through different stages include – Merker making
  • Spreading, Pattern Laying, Cutting, Bundling and Ticketing, Position Marking, Drill Marking, etc…
  •  BUNDLING & TICKETING
  • Bundling is the process of grouping cut garment components according to style, size, colour, shade and
  • production sequence.
  • One shirt bundle may contain
  • • Front, Back, Sleeve, Collar, Cuff, Pocket, Placket etc…
  • Importance
  • • Prevents component mixing.
  • • Maintains production sequence.
  • • Facilitates line feeding.
  • • Reduces missing components.
  • Ticketing means attaching identification tickets to garment bundles/components to provide production
  • information and maintain traceability.
  • Information may include
  • • Style number
  • • Size
  • • Bundle number
  • • Lot number

questions.question: Compare sea shipment and air shipment with respect to cost, speed, capacity, suitability and reliability.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare sea shipment and air shipment with respect to cost, speed, capacity, suitability and
  • reliability.
  •  Sea Transportation
  • Transportation of goods through ships and cargo vessels across seas and oceans.
  • Advantages
  • • Suitable for large quantities
  • • Lower cost per unit for international bulk shipments
  • • Suitable for containerized garment exports
  • • Ideal for long-distance international transportation
  • Disadvantages
  • • Slow compared with air transportation
  • • Dependent on port schedules
  •  Air Transportation
  • Transportation of goods using cargo aircraft or commercial aircraft cargo services.
  • Advantages
  • • Very fast
  • • Suitable for urgent shipments
  • • Long international distances can be covered quickly
  • Disadvantages
  • • Very expensive
  • • Limited cargo capacity compared with ships
